summary: Portfolio page timeouts and gateway 504s were caused by a config change (cfg-2207) at 09:52:13 that cut portfolio-service's datasource HikariCP max pool size from 50 to 5. The pool (total=5) saturated immediately under normal ~565 req/s load, producing "could not acquire JDBC connection" and HikariPool timeout errors from 09:53:19, which propagated as 3-4.5s upstream timeouts and 504s at api-gateway. The gateway HTTP/2 upgrade (dep-5220, 08:00) is a red herring: gateway latency was flat at ~206ms for 1h44m after the deploy and only jumped at ~09:44-09:48, coinciding with the pool config change (applied 09:52), not the deploy.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Config change cut portfolio-service DB pool to 5 connections, exhausting it under normal load
ranked_hypotheses.statement: cfg-2207 (infra-automation) applied a 'cost-optimisation profile small' at 09:52, reducing portfolio-service datasource HikariCP max_size from 50 to 5. Under steady ~565 req/s the 5-connection pool saturated (active=5, idle=0, waiting 25-57), requests blocked up to 3000ms and failed to acquire connections, driving portfolio latency to ~4.2s and 504s at api-gateway. Onset aligns with the config-change time, not the 08:00 gateway deploy.

causal_chain.claim: 5 connections exhausted at ~565 req/s -> HikariPool waiting=43, acquire timeout 3000ms
portfolio requests fail/slow -> 504 upstream timeouts at gateway

assumptions: The 09:44 latency uptick and 09:52 config apply are the same incident onset (config propagation/jitter explains ~1 min gap between 09:52 apply and 09:53 first error).
Pool size 5 is insufficient for the observed steady request rate; 50 was sufficient.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Gateway HTTP/2 upgrade (dep-5220) introduced the fault
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The api-gateway v9.3.0 deploy at 08:00 enabling HTTP/2 to upstreams (portfolio-service, order-service) caused upstream timeouts and 504s.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Timing contradicts: gateway p99 and error_rate were flat/normal (~206ms, 0.2% 5xx) for 1h44m after the 08:00 deploy and only degraded at ~09:44-09:48; the 504s are specifically 'upstream timeout portfolio-service' driven by portfolio pool exhaustion; gateway CPU was flat ~42%. No rollback evidence ties recovery to the deploy.

ranked_hypotheses.title: ledger-db infrastructure/IO fault (historical pattern HIST-102/HIST-110)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A ledger-db primary failover or IOPS throttling caused portfolio-service DB connection failures and downstream timeouts.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: ledger-db emitted zero WARN+ logs for 06:00-11:59, and the portfolio errors are client-side connection-acquire timeouts from a HikariPool of size exactly 5, not refused/errored DB connections. Historical similarity is only a lead, not evidence.

facts.statement: api-gateway p99 was ~206ms until 09:40, jumped to max 4418ms at 09:48 and stayed ~4300ms.
Config change cfg-2207 reduced portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 at 09:52:00Z.
portfolio-service db_pool_in_use fell to a hard cap of 5.0 connections after the change.
HikariPool reported total=5, active=5, idle=0 with waiting queues of 25-57 from 09:54:29.
portfolio-service connection-acquire errors began at 09:53:19 (264 ERROR entries).
api-gateway logged 133 'upstream timeout portfolio-service ... -> 504' warnings starting 09:53:53.
api-gateway 5xx rate rose from ~0.2% to ~7.2% at the 09:48 bucket.
Only deployment in window was dep-5220 (api-gateway v9.3.0) at 08:00:00Z, not rolled back.
portfolio-service request_rate was flat ~560-585 req/s all window (no load increase).
api-gateway CPU was flat ~42% throughout, including during the incident.
ledger-db had zero WARN+ log matches for 06:00-11:59.

assumptions: Config changes take effect near their 'changed_at' timestamp; the 09:52 apply closely precedes the 09:53 first error.
The M-shaped 09:48 latency bucket reflects the onset edge (peak 4418ms) rather than continuous degradation from 08:00.
Pool size 50 (prior value) was adequate for the steady ~565 req/s load, as evidenced by pool usage of ~12 of 50.

timeline.event: dep-5220: api-gateway v9.3.0 deployed (envoy 1.29->1.30, HTTP/2 to upstreams). Gateway remains healthy.
Last fully-healthy bucket: gateway p99 ~206ms, portfolio error_rate 0.2%, pool ~12 connections.
First degraded bucket: gateway p99 avg 1753ms/max 4418ms; gateway 5xx 2.07%.
First portfolio-service error: 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms'.
HikariPool fully saturated: total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43.
db_pool_in_use pinned at 5.0; portfolio error_rate ~22%; gateway 5xx ~7.2% steady state.
Incident INC-002 reported (portfolio page timeouts, gateway p99 high).

recommended_actions.action: Revert cfg-2207 immediately (restore portfolio-service db.pool.max_size to 50) to relieve pool exhaustion.
recommended_actions.rationale: The pool cap of 5 is the direct cause of connection-acquire timeouts and ~22% portfolio 5xx; restoring capacity should recover the service.

recommended_actions.action: Add guardrails/validation on DB pool-size config profiles so 'small' cost profiles cannot reduce pool size below observed steady-state concurrency.
recommended_actions.rationale: infra-automation applied a sub-capacity profile with no load check, mirroring a prior incident (HIST-115: pool overridden by wrong environment profile).

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on HikariPool waiting-queue depth and pool saturation rate at portfolio-service (not just gateway p99).
recommended_actions.rationale: Detected only via gateway symptoms; a pool-level alert would localize the fault faster.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT roll back dep-5220 based on this incident; verify gateway HTTP/2 upgrade separately.
recommended_actions.rationale: Timing and error semantics rule out the deploy as the cause; rolling it back would not address pool exhaustion.

data_gaps: market-data-service latency query failed (backend 503, tc-016); could not independently confirm no degradation on that downstream dependency of portfolio-service.
No ledger-db logs/DB-internal metrics were available (0 matches) to positively rule out subtle DB-side slowness, though portfolio errors are client pool-acquire timeouts, not DB refusals.
Exact propagation delay between the 09:44 latency uptick, the 09:52 config apply, and the 09:53 first error is inferred from bucket resolution (8-10 min buckets), not second-level data.
No explicit rollback/recovery test was available to confirm restoring pool size recovers the service.

findings.statement: api-gateway p99 latency was normal (~205-207ms avg) from 09:00 through 09:40, then jumped to avg 1753ms / max 4418ms in the 09:48 bucket and stayed ~4300ms through 11:59.
A config change cfg-2207 for portfolio-service set db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 at 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z (author infra-automation, 'cost-optimisation profile small').
portfolio-service log confirms the config applied at 09:52:13: 'config change cfg-2207 applied: db.pool.max_size=5'.
portfolio-service db_pool_in_use dropped from ~12 connections (08:00-09:40) to exactly 5.0 from 10:00 onward, matching the new max_size=5.

portfolio-service HikariPool errors show total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=25-57, e.g. 'HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 3000ms (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43)' starting 09:54:29.

findings.statement: portfolio-service request errors begin at 09:53:19 with 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms'; 264 ERROR entries and top pattern count 142 for that message.

findings.statement: api-gateway logs show only 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings -> 504' warnings (133 of 134 matches), first at 09:53:53 — the 504s are gateway-side timeouts waiting on portfolio-service.
api-gateway 5xx error_rate rose from ~0.2% (09:00-09:40) to avg 2.07%/max 7.74% in the 09:48 bucket and ~7.2% thereafter.
The only deployment in the window is dep-5220 for api-gateway (v9.3.0) at 08:00:00Z, enabling HTTP/2 to upstreams; status 'live', not rolled back.
portfolio-service request_rate stayed flat ~560-585 req/s across the entire window (08:00-11:59), so load did not increase.
api-gateway CPU stayed flat ~42% throughout (08:00-11:59), including during the incident — no resource exhaustion at the gateway.
portfolio-service 5xx error_rate held ~0.2% through the 09:40 bucket then jumped to avg 13.5%/max 24.02% in the 09:50 bucket and ~22% afterward.
ledger-db produced zero log matches (WARN+) for 06:00-11:59, and the DB metric path is described as a shared postgres with telemetry; no DB-side error evidence found.
